# player_volume_heterogeneity_v1 — corrected heterogeneity screen

*Generated by `volume_heterogeneity.py`; runtime 721s; 200 permutations per test; ridge lambda=1.0 on standardized inputs. Reuses `feature_lab.py` and `interactions_lab.py` unmodified (imported, never edited).*

## Why this screen exists

`player_feature_interactions_v1` (473 tests) and `player_vs_archetype_v1` (25 tests) each returned **zero** level-2 survivors. The orchestrator power diagnostic (`experiments/power_diagnostic.py`, `power_diagnostic2.py`) showed those nulls were **vacuous, not informative**: points/36 carries only 29.8% between-player signal, the smallest individual split difference detectable in points/36 for a median player is **3.89 per 36** against a measured league condition effect of **+0.38** (home), and some tested conditions barely occur. This screen keeps the harness and changes the target to VOLUME, gates rare conditions out up front, and reports a minimum detectable effect beside every observed effect.

## Protocol (as registered)

- Window 2021-2024 ONLY. Quarantine asserted on every matrix (`quarantine_audit.json`: all_pass=True, 10 matrices; cutoff 2025-01-01). 2025/2026 are never loaded.
- Targets (the core change): **minutes played**; **shot attempts / 36**; **3pt attempts / 36**; **FT attempts / 36** — NOT points.
- Battery: 19 feature columns x 18 conditions x 4 targets = **1368 tests**. Statistic: 2024 MAE(ridge[b,f,m,f x m]) - MAE(ridge[b,f,m]) — the interaction column must earn it on walk-forward 2024.
- Null: 200 within-season BLOCK permutations of the moderator/archetype ASSIGNMENT (player blocks for the 11 player traits, team blocks for the 7 archetype conditions). BH at 10% across this screen's battery; **sign-consistency across the 3 inner folds additionally required for survival** (this registration names the clause; the previous screens did not).

## Pinned decisions (fixed before results were seen)

- **Baseline per target**: shifted per-player EWMA of that target, alpha tuned on the 3 inner 2021-2023 folds only. The registered phrase admits two harness-canonical encodings for a per-36 rate (`ewma_target` = EWMA of the rate; `ratio_ewma` = the minutes-weighted ratio-of-EWMAs the committed pooled screen used); both were swept on inner folds and the **stronger** kept — the conservative direction, since a harder baseline can only make features look worse.
- **Universe reused verbatim** from `feature_lab.build_universe`: played regular-season rows, minutes >= 8, >= 5 prior same-season appearances. Identical rows to the two prior screens, so this is a like-for-like re-test with the target swapped.
- **Feature columns**: the 14 committed pooled-screen survivors on their surviving channels at their FROZEN alphas, plus the registered resurrection shortlist. Because the target is no longer a points channel, each channel-specific resurrection feature contributes ONE column, at the channel the committed pooled screen itself ranked best (lowest p, then most negative delta) — a rule read off prior artifacts, fixed before this screen's results existed. Identical columns are collapsed (3 collapsed) so multiplicity is not inflated.
- **The committed point-channel baselines are still re-derived** ({'fg3': np.float64(0.05), 'paint': np.float64(0.05), 'ft': np.float64(0.05), 'np2': np.float64(0.05)}) because several catalog builders read `ctx.baselines`; without them the feature columns would not be the ones the previous screens tested.
- **Moderator/axis EWMAs pinned at alpha 0.10**; bios/archetype definitions untouched (`features/moderators.py`, `features/archetypes.py` are read-only here).
- **NaN features/conditions** mean-filled with FIT-window means at fit time (fold fills from fold-train) — feature encoding, not imputation.

## Correction 3 — the condition-frequency gate

Every condition's occurrence rate among the 11,948 eligible universe rows was computed BEFORE any test was run. Anything under **8%** was excluded up front and is NOT reported as a null. Occurrence is defined as: binary columns -> share at the positive level; columns with a single modal value on >50% of rows -> share off the modal value; otherwise 1.0 (the condition varies on essentially every row, so there is no rarity question).

| excluded | role | kind | occurrence | reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #7 b2b_flag | feature | binary | 2.65% | occurs on 2.64% of eligible rows (< 8% gate) |

**72 tests were never run because of this gate** — in the previous screens they would have been counted as nulls.

## Correction 4 — power reporting

Every row of `screen_results.csv` carries, beside its observed effect:

- `observed_effect` — |beta_interaction|, the fitted interaction coefficient in TARGET UNITS per (1 sd feature x 1 sd condition). Directly comparable to the MDE columns.
- `mde_player` — the registered formula `2.8 * sd_within_player * sqrt(2 / (n_per_player/2))` for the **median eligible player** of that test (eligible player = >= 20 eligible rows, the level-3 naming gate). This is the INDIVIDUAL-level resolution: what a single player's conditional split would have to be for us to see it.
- `mde_pooled` — the same formula at the test's TOTAL eligible n. This is the LEVEL-2 resolution, because the pooled ridge aggregates the split across all players at once.
- `plausible_effect` — the measured per-target anchor (max of the league home split, the league rest split, and a 5%-of-mean floor), the same anchor class the diagnostic used for points (+0.38/36 home).
- `power_label` (registered, per-player MDE) and `power_label_pooled` (pooled MDE): a non-survivor is `underpowered` when MDE > 3 x plausible effect, else `null_with_power`.

**Which label to read for which claim**: the per-player MDE governs whether an INDIVIDUAL effect (level 3) could ever have been seen; the pooled MDE governs whether the LEVEL-2 pooled test could have seen a plausible effect. Both are reported so no null is stated without saying what it could have seen.

| target | plausible effect | home split | rest split | 5% floor | median within-player sd | median MDE (player) | median MDE (pooled) |

## Headline

- **1368 tests**; p <= 0.05 before correction: **119** (global-null expectation ~68.4).
- **BH(10%) passes: 0**; with the registered sign-consistency clause, **survivors: 0**; expected false among the BH passes: ~0.0.
- Tests at the permutation p-floor (0.00498): **0**. With 1368 tests, BH at 10% cannot reject anything unless at least **69** tests sit at that floor — a hard multiplicity fact of a 200-permutation null over a battery this size, and itself a power statement about the screen (see 'Screen-level power').

## Screen-level power — what this null can and cannot say

Three distinct power questions, all answered here rather than left implicit as in the previous screens:

1. **Individual resolution (level 3)**: median per-player MDE by target is in the power table above. Compare to the plausible-effect column: a ratio far above 1 means an individual conditional effect of realistic size is invisible at this sample size, whatever the p-value says.
2. **Pooled resolution (level 2)**: median pooled MDE by target. This is the number that decides whether a level-2 null is informative.
3. **Multiplicity resolution (the screen itself)**: with 1368 tests, a 200-permutation null (p-floor 0.00498) and BH at 10%, at least 69 tests must sit at the p-floor before ANY test can be rejected. Observed at the floor: 0. This is a property of the registered design, and it is the reason the per-target secondary BH column is reported alongside.

## Level 3 — named-player deviations vs chance

Naming gates (unchanged machinery, `interactions_lab.eb_level3`): n >= 20 rows, posterior |z| >= 2 after EB shrinkage (K tuned on the inner folds), and same-sign deviation in both halves of the player's 2021-2024 appearances (>= 10 rows per half).

**Chance expectation** (the comparison the previous screen omitted): under a pure null, P(|z| >= 2) = 0.0455, and the two-half sign-replication gate passes with probability between 0.25 (halves independent) and 0.5 (halves tracking the overall sign), so chance predicts between `n_evaluated x 0.0455 x 0.25` and `n_evaluated x 0.0455 x 0.5` named players. *(By this same arithmetic the previous archetype screen's 1,352 player-pattern evaluations predicted 15-31 named players by chance; it reported 2 — i.e. it found fewer than chance, which is why the comparison has to appear.)*

- Player-pattern evaluations: **1352**; **named: 0**; **chance expects 15-31**.
- Verdict: the named count is **BELOW chance** — no evidence of credible individual heterogeneity beyond noise.
